function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the temperature forecast for New York next week. We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate parameters. The function expects a URL, headers optional, timeout optional, params including latitude, longitude, elevation optional. We need to provide the URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint. The user didn't specify the exact endpoint. We can use the standard Open-Meteo API endpoint for forecast: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to provide latitude and longitude for New York City. Latitude ~ 40.7128 N, longitude ~ -74.0060 W. We also need to specify the parameters for the forecast: we want temperature for next week. The Open-Meteo API supports specifying start_date and end_date, and specifying the variables we want. For temperature, we can request "temperature_2m" variable. We also need to specify "daily" or "hourly"? For next week, we can request daily average temperatures. The API supports "daily" parameters: "temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min", "temperature_2m_mean". We can request "daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,temperature_2m_mean". We also need to specify "start_date" and "end_date" in ISO format. Next week: from tomorrow to 7 days from now? Or from next Monday? The user said "next week". We can interpret as the next 7 days starting from tomorrow. Let's compute dates: Today is 2026-06-01. Tomorrow is 2026-06-02. Next week ends on 2026-06-08. So start_date=2026-06-02, end_date=2026-06-08. We also need to specify "timezone" parameter: "America/New_York". So the params will include:

latitude: 40.7128
longitude: -74.0060
daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,temperature_2m_mean"
start_date: "2026-06-02"
end_date: "2026-06-08"
timezone: "America/New_York"

We also need to specify "format" maybe? Not necessary.

We also need to set "elevation" optional: we can leave it null.

We also need to set "headers" optional: we can leave default.

We also need to set "timeout" optional: we can leave default.

We also need to set "allow_redirects" optional: we can leave default.

We also need to set "auth" optional: we can leave null.

We also need to set "cert" optional: we can leave null.

We also need to set "cookies" optional: we can leave empty.

We also need to set "proxies" optional: we can leave empty.

We also need to set "stream" optional: we can leave false.

We also need to set "verify" optional: we can leave true.

So we call the function with:

{
url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json" },
timeout: 10.0,
params: {
latitude: 40.7128,
longitude: -74.0060,
daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,temperature_2m_mean",
start_date: "2026-06-02",

},
